summary: Settings first, because everything reads them. The limiter, the destination check and the privacy-preserving analytics are independent of each other and run in parallel. A final task wires all three into the service, the API and the application factory. Compared with the first plan, the analytics task now delivers a dedicated privacy module, and the settings and wiring tasks carry the trusted-proxy rule.
test_strategy: Each building block is unit-tested in isolation with injected time and keys; the wiring task adds API tests for the observable behaviour (429, 422, new statistics fields) and one test that reads the click table back and asserts that no address, user agent or referrer path was stored. The existing 127 tests are the regression net, with one deliberate change: the referrer test now expects the host only.

tasks.title: Hardening settings
tasks.description: Add settings for the per-minute creation and redirect limits, for trusting X-Forwarded-For (off by default) and for the domain blocklist, read from the environment with safe defaults.

tasks.title: Token-bucket rate limiter
tasks.description: An in-memory token bucket per client key with bounded state and an injectable clock.

tasks.title: Destination vetting
tasks.description: Syntactic checks that refuse non-public, disguised, self-referencing and blocklisted destinations.

tasks.title: Privacy-preserving visitor analytics
tasks.description: A privacy module producing visitor identifiers as an HMAC under a random in-memory key that rotates daily, and reducing referrers to their host. Migration 3 adds clicks.visitor_hash for that opaque identifier; the repository stores it and aggregates unique visitors per day and clicks per referrer.

tasks.title: Wire limits, vetting and analytics into the service and API
tasks.description: Limiter dependencies on the create and redirect routes keyed by the trusted client address (socket address unless a trusted proxy is declared, then the proxy-appended X-Forwarded-For entry); destination check in URL validation; anonymous visitor identifier and referrer host recorded on redirect; statistics extended; error mapping for 429 and unsafe destinations.
